CAL_AB_WHEEL_ROLLOUT.name: Ab wheel rollout
CAL_AB_WHEEL_ROLLOUT.description: Kneel with an ab wheel in both hands and roll out until the body is nearly flat, then roll back. A demanding anti-extension exercise.
goodForm: Round the upper back slightly and tuck the pelvis
Roll out slowly and stop before the back arches
Return by squeezing the abs
badForm: Let the hips sag toward the floor
Go farther than you can control

CAL_ARCH_HANG.name: Arch hang
CAL_ARCH_HANG.description: A hang with the shoulders pulled down and back and the chest pushed forward, so the body forms a slight arch. It builds grip and the strength to hold the top half of a pull-up.
goodForm: Pull the shoulder blades down and together
Push the chest forward and look slightly up
Squeeze the glutes so the hips stay in line with the body
badForm: Hang passively with the shoulders up by the ears
Bend the elbows to fake the position

CAL_ASSISTED_SQUAT.name: Assisted squat
CAL_ASSISTED_SQUAT.description: A squat where you hold a doorframe, rail or suspended handles to take some of the load. It lets you learn full depth and a steady position.
goodForm: Grip lightly and use the arms only as much as you need
Keep the whole foot on the floor
Sit down between the hips until the thighs pass parallel
badForm: Pull yourself up with the arms

CAL_BRIDGE.name: Full bridge
CAL_BRIDGE.description: Press up from the floor into an arch with straight arms and legs, supported on hands and feet. It builds spinal strength and shoulder and hip mobility.
goodForm: Push the shoulders over the hands
Straighten the arms and legs as far as you can
Spread the arch over the whole spine
badForm: Hinge only at the lower back

CAL_BRIDGE_ANGLED.name: Angled bridge
CAL_BRIDGE_ANGLED.description: A bridge with the hands on the floor and the feet raised on a low step so the body slopes down toward the head. A stepping stone to the full bridge.
goodForm: Keep the arms straight and the chest open
Push the hips toward the ceiling
Lower the hands step by step over weeks

CAL_BRIDGE_CLOSING.name: Closing the bridge
CAL_BRIDGE_CLOSING.description: From a full bridge, shift the hands closer to the feet until the hands and feet are almost together. It asks for a flexible spine and strong shoulders.
goodForm: Walk the hands toward the feet slowly
Keep the arms straight
Hold the closed position briefly

CAL_BRIDGE_HALF.name: Half bridge
CAL_BRIDGE_HALF.description: A bridge with the hands on the floor beside the head and the arms bent, pushing the hips up until the elbows are partly bent. It is a lower-range version of the full bridge.
goodForm: Keep the hands flat and the fingers pointing toward the feet
Press the hips up without locking the arms
Breathe steadily

CAL_BRIDGE_HEAD.name: Head bridge
CAL_BRIDGE_HEAD.description: Lie on your back with feet flat, lift the hips and rest lightly on the top of the head while pressing through the feet. It builds back and neck strength toward the full bridge.
goodForm: Keep most of the weight on the feet
Rest only lightly on the head
Come down slowly and stop if the neck feels any pinch
badForm: Put heavy load on the neck
Jerk in and out of the position

CAL_BRIDGE_SHORT.name: Short bridge
CAL_BRIDGE_SHORT.description: Lie on your back with the knees bent and feet flat, then raise the hips until the body forms a line from shoulders to knees. It builds glute and back strength with a small range.
goodForm: Push through the whole foot
Squeeze the glutes at the top
Keep the neck relaxed on the floor
badForm: Push the hips so high the lower back arches hard

CAL_BRIDGE_STAND_TO_STAND.name: Stand-to-stand bridge
CAL_BRIDGE_STAND_TO_STAND.description: From standing, arch back into a full bridge, then press back up to standing without touching the floor with anything except the hands and feet. The top step of the bridge line.
goodForm: Push the hips forward and reach back slowly
Reverse the movement with the same control
Keep the arms and legs strong

CAL_BRIDGE_STRAIGHT.name: Straight bridge
CAL_BRIDGE_STRAIGHT.description: Sit with the legs straight in front and the hands behind, then push the hips up so the body forms a flat table. It stretches the front of the body and works the hamstrings.
goodForm: Keep the legs straight and the toes pulled up
Push the hips up until the body is flat
Look forward or slightly back, not at your feet
badForm: Bend the knees to get up higher

CAL_BRIDGE_WALL_DOWN.name: Wall-walking bridge down
CAL_BRIDGE_WALL_DOWN.description: Stand facing away from a wall, arch backward and walk your hands down the wall toward the floor into a bridge. It teaches you to enter the full bridge under control.
goodForm: Keep the hips pushed forward
Walk the hands down slowly
Stand a short distance from the wall at first

CAL_BRIDGE_WALL_UP.name: Wall-walking bridge up
CAL_BRIDGE_WALL_UP.description: From a full bridge facing away from a wall, walk the hands up the wall until you stand, using the back and legs. It builds the strength to come out of a bridge.
goodForm: Press the hips forward as the hands climb
Walk in small steady steps
Finish standing tall

CAL_BULGARIAN_SPLIT_SQUAT.name: Bulgarian split squat
CAL_BULGARIAN_SPLIT_SQUAT.description: A split squat with the back foot resting on a bench or box behind you. The raised rear foot makes the front leg do almost all the work.
goodForm: Set the front foot far enough ahead that the shin stays near vertical
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor
Keep the hips square to the front
badForm: Put the front foot too close so the knee travels far forward

CAL_CROW_STAND.name: Crow stand
CAL_CROW_STAND.description: Squat down, place the hands on the floor, and rest the knees on the backs of the upper arms, then lift the feet. An early arm balance that trains wrist strength and balance.
goodForm: Spread the fingers and press the floor away
Lean forward until the feet lift
Look slightly ahead
badForm: Look straight down at the hands

CAL_DIP_NEGATIVE.name: Dip negative
CAL_DIP_NEGATIVE.description: Start at the top of a dip and lower yourself slowly until the shoulders are below the elbows, then step or jump back up. It builds dip strength before you can press up.
goodForm: Lower for at least three seconds
Keep the elbows tracking back and the chest slightly forward
Stop at a depth where the shoulders feel comfortable
badForm: Drop the last part of the movement
Go deeper than your shoulders allow

CAL_FL.name: Front lever
CAL_FL.description: Hang from straight arms with the whole body held straight and level, facing up. It is one of the strongest pulling skills.
goodForm: Keep the whole body in one flat line
Pull the shoulders down and hold the arms straight
Squeeze the glutes and legs together
badForm: Let the head and feet sag

CAL_FL_ADV_TUCK.name: Advanced tuck front lever
CAL_FL_ADV_TUCK.description: The tuck front lever with the hips opened so the back is flat and the knees stay bent at ninety degrees. A longer lever than the tuck.
goodForm: Open the hips until the thighs line up with the torso
Keep the back flat and the arms straight
Pull the shoulders down and back

CAL_FL_ONE_LEG.name: One-leg front lever
CAL_FL_ONE_LEG.description: A front lever with one leg straight and the other knee tucked. It sits between the advanced tuck and straddle.
goodForm: Keep the straight leg in line with the body
Hold the hips at shoulder height
Alternate which leg is extended

CAL_FL_STRADDLE.name: Straddle front lever
CAL_FL_STRADDLE.description: A front lever with the legs straight and spread wide to shorten the lever. It is a very hard hold.
goodForm: Keep the body flat and the legs straight
Open the legs as wide as needed
Hold the arms straight and the shoulders down

CAL_FL_TUCK.name: Tuck front lever
CAL_FL_TUCK.description: Hang from a bar or rings and lift the hips so the back is flat and parallel to the floor, with the knees tucked tightly. The first real lever hold.
goodForm: Keep the arms straight and pull the shoulders down
Lift the hips to the same height as the shoulders
Keep the knees close to the chest

CAL_HANDSTAND.name: Freestanding handstand
CAL_HANDSTAND.description: Balance on the hands with the body straight and the feet in the air, without a wall. Control comes from small changes in finger pressure.
goodForm: Stack wrists, shoulders, hips and ankles in a line
Press tall through the shoulders
Look between the hands
badForm: Arch the back to hold balance

CAL_HANDSTAND_CHEST_TO_WALL.name: Chest-to-wall handstand
CAL_HANDSTAND_CHEST_TO_WALL.description: Walk the feet up a wall until the chest faces it and the body is nearly straight, then hold. It teaches the right line and shoulder opening.
goodForm: Push the floor away through the shoulders
Keep the ribs tucked and the body in a straight line
Point the toes lightly against the wall
badForm: Let the shoulders sink toward the ears

CAL_HANDSTAND_HEEL_PULL.name: Handstand heel pull
CAL_HANDSTAND_HEEL_PULL.description: From a chest-to-wall handstand, lightly pull the heels off the wall and balance for a moment, then return to the wall. It teaches the balance reflex.
goodForm: Lift the heels only a little
Press the fingertips into the floor to correct balance
Return to the wall before you fall

CAL_HANDSTAND_WALL_PLANK.name: Wall plank
CAL_HANDSTAND_WALL_PLANK.description: Walk the feet up a wall from a push-up position until the body is steeply angled, with the hands under the shoulders. It builds overhead shoulder strength toward the handstand.
goodForm: Keep the arms straight and the shoulders open
Squeeze the glutes and abs
Walk up only as far as you can hold

CAL_HANGING_BENT_LEG_RAISE.name: Hanging bent-leg raise
CAL_HANGING_BENT_LEG_RAISE.description: Hang from a bar and raise the legs with a slight bend in the knees to at least hip height. Harder than the knee raise because the legs are longer.
goodForm: Raise until the thighs are above horizontal
Keep a soft bend in the knees
Lower slowly
badForm: Let the shoulders rise toward the ears

CAL_HANGING_FROG_RAISE.name: Hanging frog raise
CAL_HANGING_FROG_RAISE.description: Hang with the feet together and the knees turned out, then lift the knees high toward the chest and extend the legs upward. It trains the hips high without the full lever.
goodForm: Keep the soles of the feet together
Lift the knees past chest height
Control the way down

CAL_HANGING_KNEE_RAISE.name: Hanging knee raise
CAL_HANGING_KNEE_RAISE.description: Hang from a bar and pull the knees up toward the chest, then lower them. It moves the leg-raise work into a hang.
goodForm: Hang with the shoulders pulled slightly down
Curl the pelvis up as the knees rise
Lower without swinging

CAL_HANGING_LEG_RAISE.name: Hanging straight-leg raise
CAL_HANGING_LEG_RAISE.description: Hang from a bar and lift straight legs until the toes touch or nearly touch the bar, then lower slowly. A very strong core exercise.
goodForm: Keep the legs together and the knees locked
Curl the pelvis up at the top
Lower for a count of three
badForm: Bend the knees to finish the rep

CAL_HANGING_LEG_RAISE_PARTIAL.name: Partial hanging straight-leg raise
CAL_HANGING_LEG_RAISE_PARTIAL.description: Hang and raise straight legs only up to about forty-five degrees, then lower. It builds toward the full straight-leg raise.
goodForm: Keep the knees locked
Raise the legs to about forty-five degrees
Lower with control
badForm: Bend the knees to lift higher

CAL_HEADSTAND_WALL.name: Wall headstand
CAL_HEADSTAND_WALL.description: Kick up to a headstand against a wall with the head and both hands on the floor. A first step for getting used to being upside down.
goodForm: Form a triangle with the head and hands
Keep most of the weight on the hands
Stack the hips over the shoulders against the wall
badForm: Rest most of the weight on the neck

CAL_HSPU.name: Handstand push-up
CAL_HSPU.description: Facing a wall in a handstand, lower the head to the floor and press back to straight arms. A strict overhead pressing exercise.
goodForm: Keep the body tight and ribs tucked
Lower the head to a mat
Press up to full lockout

CAL_HSPU_CLOSE.name: Close handstand push-up
CAL_HSPU_CLOSE.description: A handstand push-up with the hands close together. It shifts the load toward the triceps and makes balance harder.
goodForm: Place the hands about a hand width apart
Keep the elbows tucked
Press to full lockout

CAL_HSPU_HALF.name: Half handstand push-up
CAL_HSPU_HALF.description: A handstand push-up against a wall with the feet raised on a box and the head lowered only partway. It builds toward the full range.
goodForm: Keep the body as straight as you can
Lower the head halfway toward the floor
Press up to straight arms

CAL_HSPU_LEVER.name: Lever handstand push-up
CAL_HSPU_LEVER.description: A handstand push-up with one arm extended sideways on a support, so most load is on the other arm. Close to the one-arm version.
goodForm: Keep the helper arm light
Lower the head slowly
Press up with a straight body

CAL_HSPU_ONE_ARM.name: One-arm handstand push-up
CAL_HSPU_ONE_ARM.description: Lower and press back up on one arm in a handstand. An elite pressing skill reached after years of training.
goodForm: Stay square to the wall
Keep the free arm out of the way
Press smoothly to lockout

CAL_HSPU_ONE_ARM_HALF.name: Half one-arm handstand push-up
CAL_HSPU_ONE_ARM_HALF.description: A one-arm handstand push-up lowered only partway, with the other hand held out to the side. A late step on the road to a one-arm handstand push-up.
goodForm: Place the working hand under the shoulder
Lower only as far as you can control
Keep the body square to the wall
badForm: Go lower than you can press back

CAL_HSPU_UNEVEN.name: Uneven handstand push-up
CAL_HSPU_UNEVEN.description: A handstand push-up with one hand on a raised block and the other on the floor, so the low arm does more work.
goodForm: Keep the shoulders level
Lower toward the low hand
Alternate which hand is raised

CAL_KNEE_RAISE_LYING.name: Lying knee raise
CAL_KNEE_RAISE_LYING.description: Lie on your back with the knees bent, then lift the thighs to vertical and lower the feet back down, keeping the knees bent.
goodForm: Keep the lower back flat on the floor
Lift the hips slightly at the top
Lower under control
badForm: Let the feet drop to the floor

CAL_KNEE_TUCK_LYING.name: Lying knee tuck
CAL_KNEE_TUCK_LYING.description: Lie on your back and pull the knees toward the chest, then lower the feet without touching the floor. The easiest step in the leg-raise line.
goodForm: Press the lower back into the floor
Bring the knees to the chest
Lower slowly and stop just above the floor

CAL_LEG_RAISE_BENT_LYING.name: Lying bent-leg raise
CAL_LEG_RAISE_BENT_LYING.description: Lift both legs together with a slight bend in the knees up to vertical, then lower slowly. A step between the knee raise and the straight-leg version.
goodForm: Press the lower back down the whole time
Keep a slight bend in the knees
Lower the legs slowly
badForm: Arch the lower back as the legs descend

CAL_LEG_RAISE_FROG_LYING.name: Lying frog raise
CAL_LEG_RAISE_FROG_LYING.description: Lie on your back with the soles of the feet together and knees out, raise the hips with the legs pushing up toward the ceiling, then lower. It adds range and tempo to the leg raise.
goodForm: Keep the soles of the feet together
Lift the hips off the floor at the top
Lower the legs slowly
badForm: Throw the legs up with momentum

CAL_LEG_RAISE_LYING.name: Lying straight-leg raise
CAL_LEG_RAISE_LYING.description: Lie on your back and lift both straight legs to vertical, then lower them to just above the floor. The core controls the full length of the legs.
goodForm: Keep the knees locked and toes pointed
Press the lower back into the floor
Lower with a count of three
badForm: Let the back arch at the bottom

CAL_LSIT.name: L-sit
CAL_LSIT.description: Support your body on straight arms with the legs straight out in front, parallel to the floor. It trains core compression and shoulder strength.
goodForm: Push the shoulders down and keep the arms locked
Keep the legs together and the knees straight
Point the toes and hold the legs level
badForm: Let the legs drop below horizontal

CAL_LSIT_FOOT_SUPPORTED.name: Foot-supported L-sit
CAL_LSIT_FOOT_SUPPORTED.description: Support yourself on parallettes or bars with one or both feet resting lightly on the floor in front. It teaches the compression and shoulder position of an L-sit.
goodForm: Press the shoulders down and lock the arms
Keep the legs straight with the heels touching the floor
Lift the weight off the feet gradually
badForm: Round the back and collapse the chest

CAL_LSIT_ONE_LEG.name: One-leg L-sit
CAL_LSIT_ONE_LEG.description: Hold an L-sit with one leg straight out in front and the other knee tucked in. It splits the demand in half.
goodForm: Keep the extended leg locked and level with the hips
Switch legs between sets
Press the floor away through the arms

CAL_LSIT_PULLUP.name: L-sit pull-up
CAL_LSIT_PULLUP.description: A strict pull-up while holding the legs straight out in front at hip height. It adds a hard core and hip-flexor demand to the pull.
goodForm: Lock the knees and point the toes
Keep the legs level with the hips for the whole rep
Pull smoothly without swinging
badForm: Let the legs sag as you tire
Swing the legs forward to gain momentum

CAL_LSIT_TUCK.name: Tuck L-sit
CAL_LSIT_TUCK.description: Hold your body off the floor on straight arms with both knees pulled toward the chest. It is an easier version of the full L-sit.
goodForm: Press down strongly through straight arms
Pull the knees to the chest
Round the upper back slightly

CAL_MUSCLEUP.name: Muscle-up
CAL_MUSCLEUP.description: Pull yourself up and over a bar or rings until you are in a straight-arm support on top. It joins a pull-up and a dip into one move.
goodForm: Pull high with the elbows driving back
Lean forward over the bar through the transition
Press to full lockout on top
badForm: Chicken-wing one arm over the bar

CAL_MUSCLEUP_BAND.name: Band-assisted muscle-up
CAL_MUSCLEUP_BAND.description: A muscle-up with a band looped under the feet or knees to reduce load. It lets you practise the transition over the bar.
goodForm: Pull high and lean the chest over the bar quickly
Move through the transition with elbows close
Press out to straight arms above the bar

CAL_NORDIC_CURL.name: Nordic curl
CAL_NORDIC_CURL.description: With the feet anchored, lower your straight body toward the floor using only the hamstrings, then pull back up. One of the hardest hamstring exercises in bodyweight training.
goodForm: Keep the hips extended and the body in one line
Lower for as long as you can control it
Catch yourself with the hands and push back up if needed
badForm: Fold at the hips to cheat the lever

CAL_NORDIC_CURL_BANDED.name: Banded Nordic curl negative
CAL_NORDIC_CURL_BANDED.description: Kneel with the feet anchored and lower the body forward as slowly as possible while a band, anchored above, takes part of your weight. It builds the strength to control a full Nordic curl.
goodForm: Keep the body straight from knee to head
Lower as slowly as you can under control
Use a thicker band if you fall in the first half
badForm: Bend at the hips instead of staying straight
Let go and drop to the floor

CAL_PALLOF_PRESS_BANDED.name: Banded Pallof press
CAL_PALLOF_PRESS_BANDED.description: Stand sideways to a band anchored at chest height, press your hands straight out and bring them back without letting the band turn you. It trains the trunk to resist rotation.
goodForm: Stand tall with the hips and shoulders square
Press the hands straight in front of the chest
Pause with arms extended before returning
badForm: Let the band pull the torso around

CAL_PISTOL.name: Pistol squat
CAL_PISTOL.description: Squat to full depth on one leg with the other leg held straight in front, then stand back up. It needs strength, balance and mobility.
goodForm: Keep the free leg straight and off the floor
Let the arms reach forward for balance
Drive up through the heel with the chest tall
badForm: Drop into the bottom without control

CAL_PISTOL_ASSISTED.name: Assisted pistol squat
CAL_PISTOL_ASSISTED.description: A full-depth one-leg squat where you hold a support or a band with the hands to take away some load. It lets you train the full range before doing it unaided.
goodForm: Hold the support lightly with straight arms
Keep the free leg off the floor
Sit all the way to the bottom and rise smoothly
badForm: Pull yourself up on the support

CAL_PLANCHE_ADV_TUCK.name: Advanced tuck planche
CAL_PLANCHE_ADV_TUCK.description: A tuck planche with the back flat and the knees still bent, a longer lever than the tuck.
goodForm: Open the hips so the back is flat
Keep the arms straight
Hold the shoulders far over the hands

CAL_PLANCHE_LEAN.name: Planche lean
CAL_PLANCHE_LEAN.description: In a straight-arm plank, shift the shoulders far forward of the hands while keeping the body straight. It builds the wrist and shoulder strength of a planche.
goodForm: Keep the arms locked and the shoulders pushing down
Lean forward until the shoulders are well past the hands
Keep the body in a straight line

CAL_PLANCHE_STRADDLE.name: Straddle planche
CAL_PLANCHE_STRADDLE.description: A planche held with the legs straight and spread wide. It needs very strong shoulders, wrists and core.
goodForm: Keep the legs straight and wide
Hold the body flat and level
Push strongly through the shoulders

CAL_PLANCHE_TUCK.name: Tuck planche
CAL_PLANCHE_TUCK.description: Balance on straight arms with the feet off the floor and the knees tucked in, the hips about level with the shoulders. The first hold where the whole body is off the ground.
goodForm: Lock the arms and push the shoulders forward
Round the back and tuck the knees tight
Keep the hips at shoulder height
badForm: Let the hips rise too high

CAL_PLANK.name: Plank
CAL_PLANK.description: Hold the body straight on forearms and toes. It trains the trunk to resist sagging.
goodForm: Stack the elbows under the shoulders
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the ribs down
Breathe steadily without letting the hips drop
badForm: Raise the hips into a pike

CAL_PULLUP.name: Pull-up
CAL_PULLUP.description: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and pull until your chin clears it, then lower to straight arms. A basic test of upper-body pulling strength.
goodForm: Begin each rep from a dead hang with the shoulders set down
Pull the elbows down and back, chest toward the bar
Lower under control to full extension
badForm: Crane the neck forward to reach the bar

CAL_PULLUP_BAND_ASSISTED.name: Band-assisted pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_BAND_ASSISTED.description: A pull-up with a resistance band looped around the bar and under a foot or knee. The band helps most at the bottom, letting you practise full pull-ups before you can do them unassisted.
goodForm: Start every rep from straight arms and shoulders pulled down
Pull the elbows toward the ribs
Move to a thinner band as you get stronger
badForm: Bounce out of the bottom on the band
Stop short of getting the chin over the bar

CAL_PULLUP_CHEST_TO_BAR.name: Chest-to-bar pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_CHEST_TO_BAR.description: A strict pull-up where the chest touches the bar. It teaches the pull height needed for a muscle-up.
goodForm: Pull until the chest touches the bar
Lean back slightly at the top
Lower to a full hang
badForm: Reach the chin to the bar only

CAL_PULLUP_CLOSE.name: Close-grip pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_CLOSE.description: A pull-up with the hands touching or nearly touching. The narrow grip loads the biceps and lats more.
goodForm: Grip with the hands a few centimetres apart
Pull the chest toward the bar
Lower to full extension
badForm: Pull the chin forward to the bar

CAL_PULLUP_HALF.name: Half pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_HALF.description: A pull-up lifted only about halfway, until the elbows reach ninety degrees. It builds strength in the lower half of the movement.
goodForm: Start from a full hang with shoulders set
Pull until the elbows are bent about ninety degrees
Lower to straight arms
badForm: Cut the hang short at the bottom

CAL_PULLUP_HIGH.name: High pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_HIGH.description: A strict pull-up pulled as high as possible, until the bar reaches the upper chest. It builds the strength to bring the body above the bar.
goodForm: Pull the elbows back behind the body
Aim the bar toward the sternum
Keep the legs together and body tight
badForm: Stop with the chin at the bar

CAL_PULLUP_JACKKNIFE.name: Jackknife pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_JACKKNIFE.description: Hang from a bar with the feet on a raised support in front, hips bent, and pull the chest toward the bar. The legs share the weight, making it easier than a full pull-up.
goodForm: Place the feet on a bench in front of you
Pull the chest toward the bar
Lower to straight arms each rep
badForm: Stop with the elbows still bent

CAL_PULLUP_NEGATIVE.name: Pull-up negative
CAL_PULLUP_NEGATIVE.description: Jump or step up so your chin is over the bar, then lower yourself as slowly as you can to straight arms. Lowering is easier than pulling, so this builds the strength for the first pull-up.
goodForm: Start with the chin above the bar and the shoulders down
Take at least three seconds to lower
Finish in a full dead hang before the next rep
badForm: Drop quickly through the lower half
Start with the head poked forward over the bar

CAL_PULLUP_ONE_ARM.name: One-arm pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_ONE_ARM.description: Pull the chin over a bar using one arm only. It is one of the hardest bodyweight pulling skills.
goodForm: Start from a dead hang with the shoulder set
Pull the elbow down toward the hip
Lower smoothly to full extension
badForm: Loosen the grip at the bottom

CAL_PULLUP_ONE_ARM_ASSISTED.name: Assisted one-arm pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_ONE_ARM_ASSISTED.description: A one-arm pull-up with a light assist such as a towel, band or the free hand gripping a lower point. It lets you practise the full range.
goodForm: Keep the assisting hand as light as possible
Pull the elbow toward the ribs
Lower slowly to a full hang
badForm: Let the helper do the work

CAL_PULLUP_ONE_ARM_HALF.name: Half one-arm pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_ONE_ARM_HALF.description: A one-arm pull-up taken only about halfway up, with the other hand held lightly on the wrist or released. A major step toward the full one-arm pull-up.
goodForm: Hold the working wrist firmly with the free hand only for balance
Pull until the elbow reaches ninety degrees
Lower under control
badForm: Use the free hand to pull

CAL_PULLUP_UNEVEN.name: Uneven pull-up
CAL_PULLUP_UNEVEN.description: A pull-up with one hand on the bar and the other holding a towel or lower rung, so one arm does more work. It builds toward the one-arm pull-up.
goodForm: Let the upper hand do most of the work
Keep the shoulders level
Switch which hand is higher each set
badForm: Pull hard with the helping hand

CAL_PULL_VERTICAL.name: Vertical pull
CAL_PULL_VERTICAL.description: Hold a fixed upright post or doorframe edge with both hands and lean back, then pull yourself back to upright. The easiest pulling step, with the body close to vertical.
goodForm: Grip the support firmly and lean back with a straight body
Pull the elbows toward the ribs
Lower back slowly to straight arms
badForm: Pull with the shoulders shrugged up

CAL_PUSHUP.name: Push-up
CAL_PUSHUP.description: From a straight-arm plank, lower the chest to just above the floor and press back up with the body held rigid. The standard horizontal push.
goodForm: Hands under the shoulders and body in one line
Elbows at about 45 degrees from the ribs
Touch the chest down and lock the arms out
badForm: Let the hips sag or rise

CAL_PUSHUP_CLOSE.name: Close push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_CLOSE.description: A push-up with the hands a few centimetres apart, narrower than the shoulders. A step toward harder single-arm work.
goodForm: Place the hands just inside shoulder width
Keep the elbows brushing the sides
Lower under control and press to lockout

CAL_PUSHUP_DIAMOND.name: Diamond push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_DIAMOND.description: A push-up with the hands close together under the chest, forming a diamond with the thumbs and index fingers. It shifts the load toward the triceps.
goodForm: Keep the elbows tucked close to the ribs
Lower the chest to the hands
Brace the core so the hips stay level

CAL_PUSHUP_HALF.name: Half push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_HALF.description: A push-up where you go down only about halfway, until the upper arms are parallel to the floor. It builds toward the full range.
goodForm: Lower until the elbows reach about ninety degrees
Hold the plank position the whole time
Lock out at the top

CAL_PUSHUP_INCLINE.name: Incline push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_INCLINE.description: A push-up with the hands on a bench, step or bar so the body slopes down toward the feet. Lower the surface over time to make it harder.
goodForm: Keep the body in one straight line
Lower the chest to the edge of the support
Point the elbows about 45 degrees from the torso
badForm: Let the hips sag or pike

CAL_PUSHUP_KNEELING.name: Kneeling push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_KNEELING.description: A push-up from the knees, with a straight line from knees to head. It shortens the lever so you can practise a full range on the floor.
goodForm: Keep the hips extended with a straight line from knees to head
Lower the chest to the floor
Press all the way to straight arms
badForm: Sit the hips back toward the heels

CAL_PUSHUP_LEVER.name: Lever push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_LEVER.description: A push-up with one arm straight out to the side and sliding on a towel or support, so most of your weight is on the other arm. A bridge to the true one-arm push-up.
goodForm: Keep the supporting arm slightly bent and under the chest
Let the straight arm help only as much as you need
Lower the chest to the floor under control

CAL_PUSHUP_ONE_ARM.name: One-arm push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_ONE_ARM.description: A push-up using only one arm, with the feet wide and the free hand behind the back. It needs strong pressing muscles and a very tight core.
goodForm: Place the feet wider than the shoulders
Keep the hips and shoulders square to the floor
Press the floor away smoothly until the arm is locked
badForm: Twist the body open as you tire
Jerk up out of the bottom

CAL_PUSHUP_ONE_ARM_HALF.name: Half one-arm push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_ONE_ARM_HALF.description: A one-arm push-up lowered only halfway, with the feet wide for balance. It builds toward the full one-arm push-up.
goodForm: Set the feet wide and keep the hips square
Tuck the working elbow near the ribs
Lower to ninety degrees and press up
badForm: Collapse the shoulder at the bottom

CAL_PUSHUP_PSEUDO_PLANCHE.name: Pseudo planche push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_PSEUDO_PLANCHE.description: A push-up with the hands placed by the hips and the shoulders leaned well forward of them. It loads the front shoulders and prepares you for planche work.
goodForm: Turn the fingers outward and put the hands near the waist
Lean the shoulders far over the hands
Keep the body straight and the shoulder blades spread
badForm: Let the hips pike up to cut the load
Hold the lean with bent arms and a sagging chest

CAL_PUSHUP_UNEVEN.name: Uneven push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_UNEVEN.description: A push-up with one hand on a raised surface such as a ball or block and the other on the floor. The lower hand does most of the pressing.
goodForm: Keep the shoulders level
Lean toward the lower hand as you descend
Switch which hand is raised between sets
badForm: Use the raised hand to push off hard

CAL_PUSHUP_WALL.name: Wall push-up
CAL_PUSHUP_WALL.description: Face a wall with arms straight and hands at chest height, then bend the elbows to bring the chest to the wall and push back. The gentlest push-up variation.
goodForm: Stand a bit more than an arm length away
Keep the body straight from head to heels
Lower until the nose nearly touches the wall
badForm: Flare the elbows straight out to the sides

CAL_RDL_BODYWEIGHT.name: Bodyweight Romanian deadlift
CAL_RDL_BODYWEIGHT.description: Push the hips back with soft knees and lower the torso until you feel the hamstrings stretch, then stand tall. It teaches the hip hinge without weight.
goodForm: Keep the back flat and the knees softly bent
Send the hips straight back like closing a door with them
Squeeze the glutes to stand up
badForm: Turn it into a squat by bending the knees a lot

CAL_REVERSE_HYPEREXTENSION.name: Reverse hyperextension
CAL_REVERSE_HYPEREXTENSION.description: Lie face down over the edge of a bench or box and swing the straight legs up behind you until they are in line with the body. It strengthens the glutes and lower back with little spinal load.
goodForm: Hold the bench firmly and keep the torso still
Lift the legs by squeezing the glutes
Lower slowly without swinging
badForm: Arch the lower back past neutral at the top

CAL_RING_ROLLOUT.name: Ring ab rollout
CAL_RING_ROLLOUT.description: Kneel holding low rings and roll forward until the arms are extended, then pull back to the start. The rings move freely, so the core works hard to stay stable.
goodForm: Tuck the pelvis and keep a straight line from knees to head
Reach only as far as you can keep the back flat
Pull back with the abs rather than the hips
badForm: Let the lower back arch at full reach
Fold at the hips to come back

CAL_ROW_ARCHER.name: Archer row
CAL_ROW_ARCHER.description: On a wide grip, pull to one side while the opposite arm stays straight like a bowstring, then alternate. It prepares you for one-arm pulling.
goodForm: Pull toward the working hand and keep the other arm straight
Keep the hips level and the body rigid
Control the lowering to the center
badForm: Twist the torso to reach the bar

CAL_ROW_HORIZONTAL.name: Horizontal row
CAL_ROW_HORIZONTAL.description: Lie under a bar or rings with the body straight and parallel to the floor, then pull the chest up to your hands. Also called an inverted row.
goodForm: Keep the legs, hips and chest in one plank-like line
Pull the shoulder blades back first
Touch the chest to the bar or rings

CAL_ROW_INCLINE.name: Incline row
CAL_ROW_INCLINE.description: A row with the body leaning back at about 45 degrees under a bar or rings. A middle step between vertical and horizontal rows.
goodForm: Hold the body straight from heels to head
Pull the chest toward the hands
Lower to straight arms with control

CAL_ROW_VERTICAL.name: Vertical row
CAL_ROW_VERTICAL.description: Stand holding rings or a bar and lean back only slightly, then pull yourself to upright. With an almost vertical body the load is small, so it suits a first rowing practice.
goodForm: Keep the body in a straight line
Pull the elbows back and squeeze the shoulder blades
Walk the feet forward to make it harder
badForm: Shrug the shoulders toward the ears

CAL_ROW_WIDE.name: Wide row
CAL_ROW_WIDE.description: A horizontal row with a wider grip and the elbows flaring out. It shifts the work toward the upper back and rear shoulders.
goodForm: Take a grip clearly wider than the shoulders
Lead with the elbows, pointing them outward
Keep the body straight and tight
badForm: Pull with the neck and shoulders only
Let the hips rise or sag

CAL_SCAPULAR_PULL.name: Scapular pull
CAL_SCAPULAR_PULL.description: Hang from a bar with straight arms and pull only your shoulder blades down, lifting the body a few centimetres. It teaches the shoulder position every pull-up starts from.
goodForm: Keep the elbows locked straight the whole time
Drive the shoulders away from the ears, then let them rise slowly
Pause for a second at the top of each rep
badForm: Bend the elbows to help the movement
Swing or kick to get the body moving

CAL_SHRIMP_SQUAT_ADVANCED.name: Advanced shrimp squat
CAL_SHRIMP_SQUAT_ADVANCED.description: The full shrimp squat, with the rear leg held behind and the torso kept upright while the knee touches down. It asks for strong quads and good ankle and hip mobility.
goodForm: Keep the chest tall and the rear foot held high
Lower with control until the knee just touches
Press up through the heel of the standing foot
badForm: Use momentum from the back leg to rise

CAL_SHRIMP_SQUAT_BEGINNER.name: Beginner shrimp squat
CAL_SHRIMP_SQUAT_BEGINNER.description: Stand on one leg, hold the other foot behind you and lower the back knee to the floor, using a light support if needed. The entry point to single-leg knee-bend strength.
goodForm: Hold a wall or post lightly for balance
Reach the back knee down gently toward the floor
Keep the standing heel planted
badForm: Drop the last few centimetres onto the knee
Lean far forward to stay balanced

CAL_SHRIMP_SQUAT_INTERMEDIATE.name: Intermediate shrimp squat
CAL_SHRIMP_SQUAT_INTERMEDIATE.description: A shrimp squat with the rear foot held in the hand and no support. The balance and range of motion are both larger than in the beginner version.
goodForm: Hold the rear foot close to the glute
Touch the back knee lightly to a mat each rep
Stand up without pushing off the back leg
badForm: Rest the full weight on the rear knee
Let the standing knee roll inward

CAL_SINGLE_LEG_DEADLIFT.name: Single-leg deadlift
CAL_SINGLE_LEG_DEADLIFT.description: Hinge forward on one leg while the other extends straight behind you, then return upright. It builds hamstring strength and hip balance.
goodForm: Keep the hips level and pointed at the floor
Reach the free leg back in line with the torso
Soften the standing knee and keep the foot flat
badForm: Open the hips to the side
Round the back to reach lower

CAL_SPLIT_SQUAT.name: Split squat
CAL_SPLIT_SQUAT.description: Take a long stance with one foot forward and lower the back knee toward the floor, then press back up. It trains one leg at a time without the balance demand of a lunge step.
goodForm: Keep the torso upright and the front foot flat
Lower straight down rather than forward
Drive up through the whole front foot
badForm: Let the front knee cave inward
Shorten the stance so the heel lifts

CAL_SQUAT.name: Bodyweight squat
CAL_SQUAT.description: Stand with feet about shoulder width and sit down until the thighs are at least level with the floor, then stand back up. The base movement for every leg progression.
goodForm: Push the knees out over the middle toes
Keep the heels down and the chest up
Reach full hip extension at the top

CAL_SQUAT_CLOSE.name: Close squat
CAL_SQUAT_CLOSE.description: A full squat with the feet together. The narrow stance demands more ankle and quad work and keeps the balance tricky.
goodForm: Keep the feet touching or nearly touching
Sit straight down and keep the heels planted
Hold the arms forward for balance
badForm: Let the heels come off the floor

CAL_SQUAT_HALF.name: Half squat
CAL_SQUAT_HALF.description: A squat that stops when the thighs are about halfway to level, with the arms out in front. It builds control through the upper range.
goodForm: Lower until the knees are at about ninety degrees
Keep the heels flat and the chest up
Drive up through the whole foot

CAL_SQUAT_JACKKNIFE.name: Jackknife squat
CAL_SQUAT_JACKKNIFE.description: A deep squat with the torso folded forward and the hands on the floor in front for support. It builds leg strength in the bottom range with the arms sharing the load.
goodForm: Fold forward with the chest close to the thighs
Keep the hands light on the floor
Stand fully upright between reps
badForm: Push off the floor with the hands

CAL_SQUAT_ONE_LEG_HALF.name: Half one-leg squat
CAL_SQUAT_ONE_LEG_HALF.description: A one-leg squat that stops halfway down while the free leg reaches forward. It builds balance and strength for the full one-leg squat.
goodForm: Extend the free leg in front and keep it off the floor
Lower until the thigh is halfway to level
Keep the standing heel flat
badForm: Fall back onto the free foot

CAL_SQUAT_SHOULDERSTAND.name: Shoulderstand squat
CAL_SQUAT_SHOULDERSTAND.description: Lie on your back with the legs in the air and the hands on the floor, then bend and straighten the knees toward the chest. A gentle first leg step that loads the quads without balance demands.
goodForm: Keep the hips up and the weight on the shoulders
Bend the knees until the thighs near the chest
Push back to straight legs without swinging
badForm: Pull on the neck with the hands

CAL_SQUAT_SUPPORTED.name: Supported squat
CAL_SQUAT_SUPPORTED.description: A full squat holding a fixed object in front for balance. You use the grip to stay upright and keep the heels down.
goodForm: Hold something steady at chest height
Sit between the hips to full depth
Use the arms only for balance
badForm: Hang from the support to stand up

CAL_SQUAT_UNEVEN.name: Uneven squat
CAL_SQUAT_UNEVEN.description: A squat with one foot flat on the floor and the other raised on a small step, so the lower leg takes more of the load. A step toward one-leg squats.
goodForm: Place the raised foot only a few centimetres higher
Keep both feet pointing forward
Switch legs between sets
badForm: Shift sideways over the low leg

CAL_SUPPORT_HOLD.name: Support hold
CAL_SUPPORT_HOLD.description: Hold your body up on straight arms between two bars, parallettes or rings. It builds the lockout strength and shoulder stability needed for dips.
goodForm: Lock the elbows and press the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the chest tall and the legs together
Breathe steadily and keep the body still
badForm: Shrug the shoulders up toward the ears
Let the elbows bend or flare
